title: Multivariate-normal MLE with incomplete data
procedure: Maximum-likelihood estimation of the mean vector mu and covariance matrix Sigma of a multivariate normal distribution from data with arbitrary item-level missingness (missing-at-random). Each observation contributes the marginal log-likelihood over its observed coordinates; the estimator maximizes the summed observed-data log-likelihood. Entry point: mlest(data, *, method='direct'|'em'|'monotone', backend='cpu'|'gpu'|'gpu_fp64'|'auto', solver=None, force=False, ...) -> MVNSolution.
algorithms: Forward-Cholesky parameterization of Sigma: the optimizer works in the unconstrained space of a Cholesky factor, so every iterate is positive-definite by construction (no projection/repair step). This is the contribution the mvnmle paper formalizes.

Default CPU path: a fast PyTorch forward-Cholesky estimator in fp64 (deterministic), which matches R to ~1e-9 and beats R by ~90-390x. solver='reference' selects the R-exact numpy inverse-Cholesky path (no PyTorch), the validation anchor.

GPU backends: CUDA and Apple-Metal (MPS) run the same forward-Cholesky estimator in fp32 (a single fused objective/gradient pass per iteration); gpu_fp64 is CUDA-only (Metal has no fp64). GPU reductions are fp32, so estimates are not bit-reproducible across runs.

Degeneracy guards (fail-loud, Rule 1): a (near-)constant / zero-variance column is rejected at the input boundary (no interior MLE exists); a rank-deficient fitted covariance (near-collinear columns) is rejected via the scale-invariant correlation-matrix minimum-eigenvalue test. force=True downgrades both refusals to a warning + converged=False.
Trace-term evaluation has two backends (direct solve vs blocked) selected per device; gradients via analytic form or autodiff (see the factorial study).

reference.name: R mvnmle
reference.what: The CRAN mvnmle package, which maximizes the same observed-data likelihood using an inverse-Cholesky parameterization in fp64. It is the established reference implementation; agreement in loglik and in the estimated mu/Sigma summaries (Frobenius norm, log-determinant) is the correctness claim.
also_compared: semopy (Python SEM, on the GSS survey)

tolerances.loglik_vs_r: CPU (fp64) agrees with R to fp64 round-off: |Delta loglik|/|loglik| ~ 1e-4 to 1e-9 across GSS/WVS at p=15-25 (relative agreement tightens on better-conditioned data; WVS reaches ~6e-10).
tolerances.gpu_fp32_tolerance: The fp32 GPU path is an EXPLICIT opt-in whose accuracy is the fp32 arithmetic floor for the problem, NOT fp64 round-off. Measured (CUDA + MPS) on the standardized GSS/WVS regime: covariance Frobenius error (rel_fro) is near-machine-fp32 (~2e-4) on well-conditioned data (WVS, cond~1e2), and rises with conditioning to a few percent on moderately ill-conditioned data (GSS, cond~1e3: ~3-9% rel_fro; loglik relDelta ~1e-3). This is disclosed via backend_name='gpu_*_fp32'; for a full-precision covariance use the CPU backend. (This replaces the earlier, over-optimistic 'differs in the last digit of mu/Sigma' claim.)
tolerances.gpu_no_silent_wrong: The fp32 GPU path is a true safe-side classifier (R12/R13, proven on CUDA first): it never returns a fit wronger than the fp32 floor, and at the ill-conditioned boundary it REFUSES (the fp32 accept-set is a subset of the fp64 accept-set) rather than silently accepting a degraded fit. Refusal is loud (SingularMatrixError on a rank-deficient fitted covariance, or NumericalError on an ill-conditioned sample covariance, e.g. 'scale your data before fitting').

limitations: R mvnmle does not run past roughly p = 50 in practical time; head-to-head agreement is therefore established at p <= 25 and the high-p story is internal (CPU vs GPU).

GPU paths are fp32 (fp64 only on CUDA via backend='gpu_fp64'); the fp32 covariance error grows with conditioning and problem size (up to a few percent), so for full-precision covariance use the CPU backend. The GPU path is a speed play (7.4x over CPU at p=50) with a disclosed precision cost, kept only where it wins.
Assumes missing-at-random; the estimator does not model a missingness mechanism.

The MLE requires a non-degenerate observed-data covariance. Near-collinear columns (rank-deficient covariance) and (near-)constant / zero-variance columns have no interior MLE and are rejected loudly (SingularMatrixError); pass force=True to obtain the degenerate result with converged=False.

audit.intro: Constitutional-compliance audit (R4) of the public surface at 4.6.13. mlest uses the canonical selector taxonomy: backend= encodes device+precision only ('cpu'/'gpu'/'gpu_fp64'/'auto', no use_fp64); method= is the estimation algorithm ('direct'/'em'/'monotone'); solver= is the numerical routine, with solver='reference' selecting the R-exact numpy inverse-Cholesky path. Results are MVNSolution objects with muhat/sigmahat/loglik/converged/n_iter/correlation_matrix/standard_deviations/aic/bic/backend_name/warnings accessors. Errors use core.exceptions (ValidationError, SingularMatrixError, NumericalError). The v3.18.0 report documented the pre-4.0 API (use_fp64/maxit/m); those names no longer exist publicly and this report supersedes it.
audit.gpu_reconciliation: The fp32 GPU path estimates and inverts per-pattern covariance blocks in single precision -- the CF-1 exposure class (an fp32 covariance path an optimizer can drive into the ill-conditioned regime) that materialised silently-wrong in ordinal/multinomial and gam. Unlike those, mvnmle does NOT form an X'WX Hessian for standard errors (it returns mu/Sigma/loglik only), and the fp32 path was proven a true safe-side classifier on CUDA (authoritative) + MPS: across a controlled condition-number sweep (kappa 1e1..1e9) and the real GSS/WVS regime, the fp32 accept-set is always a subset of the fp64 accept-set (at kappa=1e6 fp64 accepts, fp32 refuses; on raw-scale survey data cond~1.5e12 fp32 refuses with 'scale your data', fp64 accepts) -- never the dangerous direction. The audit's flagged |Delta loglik| 113-146 at GSS p=20-25 decomposes as real fp32 arithmetic-floor error (deficit ~ report_gap; evaluation noise negligible), not a silent-wrong. No R16 showstopper; the version floor is not raised by mvnmle.

findings.title: constant-column silently accepted by the default call
findings.detail: The naive mlest(X) on a (near-)constant / zero-variance column returned converged=True with a meaningless, arbitrarily-large loglik and no warning -- the scale-invariant fitted-covariance guard cannot see a zero-variance column (it divides each variable by its own std). Fixed by an input-boundary guard (check_observed_variances) that rejects any column whose observed values span <= 1e-10 x scale, raising SingularMatrixError (force=True -> converged=False + warning), mirroring the collinearity guard. Genuinely small-but-varying columns are unaffected. Found via the R15 default-invocation / R10 hard-case grid.

findings.title: fp32 GPU tolerance documentation understated the real error
findings.detail: The v3.18.0 report claimed GPU fp32 'may differ in the last reported digit of mu/Sigma' and '~1e-4 relative on loglik'. The measured reality is up to ~9% covariance rel_fro / ~1e-3 loglik on moderately ill-conditioned large-n data -- the fp32 arithmetic floor, not last-digit. The tolerances section now states the honest fp32 magnitude and its dependence on conditioning. No code change: the fp32 path behaves as fp32 must and is a disclosed opt-in.

findings.title: backend='cpu-reference' was a non-canonical backend value
findings.detail: The R-exact reference optimizer was selected via backend='cpu-reference', overloading the backend= axis (reserved for device+precision). The canonical selector is now solver='reference'; backend='cpu-reference' remains as a deprecated alias (DeprecationWarning) and will be removed in a future major release.

datasets.name: WVS
datasets.what: World Values Survey -- continuous/ordinal items, ~97k respondents, item-level missingness; large real survey, well-conditioned after standardization (cond~1e2).

datasets.name: GSS
datasets.what: General Social Survey -- ~75k respondents; fewer but structurally different missingness patterns than WVS, moderately ill-conditioned after standardization (cond~1e3), the regime that exercises the fp32 floor.
